Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 96, English)
The Third Eye Batch, Day Three: Guru Parampara, the Discipline of Sadhna, and Why India's Spiritual Power Endures

This session is the thir d day of the same ongoing "Thir d Eye" (T eesri Aankh) advanced batch intr oduced in the pr evious session (which cover ed Day One's orientation and Day T wo's Shiva T attva/dimension teaching). This session opens with attendance discipline and a final sankalp (r esolve) r oll call for an 1 1-day sadhna cycle, followed by teaching on aligning with the guru parampara (lineage), practical rules for the sadhna, and a br oader teaching on why the speaker believes India's spiritual tradition r emains vital today . It has its own fr esh opening and its own natural close, so it is tr eated as a distinct session fr om the pr evious one, though it continues the same multi-day batch curriculum. Given the substantial live back-and-forth, it is pr esented as a 3-part document.

1. Discipline Warning: Compliance With Stated Rules Is Requir ed for Continued Support The session opens with the speaker telling an unnamed devotee that if they do not follow the rules already given to them, he cannot continue to help them — reminding the batch that he stated from the first video that he would be strict with this particular batch given the seriousness of what they have already been shown.

2. Attendance Check: Only Those Who Watched the Orientation Video May Continue The speaker conducts a roll call to confirm who has watched the required first-day orientation video; several devotees who had not received or watched it (due to a group-add delay) are told they will be sent the video personally , while a handful of others who are confirmed not ready are told plainly they do not need to do this particular sadhna and should join a future batch instead.

3. Rule Reminder: No Food After 6 P .M., Per Orientation Guidelines A devotee checks in that they ate dinner roughly 15–20 minutes before the session began; the speaker treats this lightly but reaf firms that the no-food-after -6-p.m. guideline from the orientation video stands.

4. Batch Size and Announcement: No Further Sankalp After Today The speaker notes that roughly 41–50 devotees are participating in this batch (compared to around 87 in the first and fourth batches, described as comparatively small), and announces that today is the last day new sankalp will be accepted — a message is to be posted informing the group that only those who complete today's sankalp will receive this cycle's aligned spiritual ener gies for the following 1 1 days.

5. Compr ehension Check: Reviewing Day One and Day Two's Teaching The speaker checks whether the batch understood the previous two days' teaching: Day One covered orientation and an introduction to four deities (not re-named in this session, to be covered again for those who missed it in a future batch), and Day Two covered an electron-proton-neutron analogy used to explain the existence of the Earth and, by extension, the existence of God.

6. Pr omise: Completing This Sadhna Eleven Times Brings Pr ofound Per ception The speaker promises that if a devotee completes this 1 1-day sadhna a full eleven times, they will begin to perceive a person's past, present, and future simply by looking at them, understand others' thoughts, and see their own jaap and tapasya (austerity) produce results almost instantly .

7. Warning: Post-Mahotsav Powers Are Mor e Intense ("Ugra") Than Befor e The speaker warns that the spiritual ener gies now being connected to this batch have been "upgraded" since Mahotsav , with many newly-involved saints described as fierce (ugra) and highly powerful.

8. Teaching: Ashaeiynn Wants Only a Devotee's Time and Sincer e Devotion, Not Money The speaker reiterates that nothing material is required of devotees in this batch — only their time and their genuine devotional feeling (bhaav) toward their guru and the connected spiritual powers — promising that in return, these powers will remain fully aligned with and available to a sincere practitioner .

9. Warning: Insincerity Cannot Be Hidden Fr om These Powers The speaker warns against outwardly professing devotion ("nothing is above Baba for me") while privately doubting, citing a devotional couplet to the ef fect that Ram and Hanuman ji know a person's past, present, and future just as well as the devotee is asking to know others' — so insincerity , described metaphorically as "changing color like a chameleon," will not go undetected.

10. Q&A: When Does the First Day of the Sadhna Officially Begin? A devotee asks whether jaap done tonight (after sankalp but before the formal start) counts toward the sadhna. The speaker clarifies that today is only for taking sankalp; the first of ficial day of the 1 1-day sadhna begins the following morning.

1 1. Q&A: Must the Four Hours of Daily Jaap Be Done in One Continuous Sitting? A devotee asks whether the four hours must be completed in one unbroken session at night, or can be split (e.g., some in the morning). The speaker confirms flexibility — a devotee may split their four hours across the day as suits them, doing "as much as you wish, however you wish."

12. Rule: The Diya (Lamp) Must Remain Lit Fr om Start to End of Each Day's Practice The speaker confirms that the lamp lit for this sadhna should remain burning continuously from the start of the day's prayer through its completion.

13. Clarification: Other Ashaeiynn Sessions (Negativity Checks, Shaktipat, Havan) May Still Be Joined The speaker confirms that devotees undertaking this sadhna may still participate in other regular Ashaeiynn sessions (aura-checking, shaktipat, havan) during the 1 1-day period, and that time spent in those sessions does not need to be counted within the four hours of dedicated sadhna jaap.

14. Sankalp Roll Call: A Formal Attendance and Commitment Pr ocess The speaker conducts a formal roll call of participating devotees by name to confirm their commitment before leading the group in the sankalp (resolve) prayer for this cycle of sadhna.

15. Teaching: The Two-Part Sankalp Prayer — Inclusion and Guru Parampara The speaker teaches that only two specific prayers need to be recited during sankalp: first, a request (with Parikshit Bhaiya as witness, addressed to Hanuman ji Maharaj) to be included in Bhaiya's own sankalp; and second, a request to be connected to the guru parampara (lineage) — no additional prayer , including any formal dedication of one's jaap, needs to be separately recited, since that follows automatically from participating in the sankalp.

16. Teaching: Fr om This Point, a Practitioner's Power Is the Guru Parampara, Not Their Own Mantra The speaker teaches that up to now , devotees' spiritual power has been their personal mantra practice; from this sadhna onward, a Third Eye batch practitioner's power becomes their connection to the guru parampara (lineage) itself — meaning an entire line of gurus and saints stands behind and works through the practitioner , not the practitioner's own isolated ef fort.

17. Teaching: You Receive According to the Devotion (Bhaav) You Bring The speaker teaches that whatever devotional attitude (bhaav) a practitioner brings to this sadhna is what they will receive back from it — sincere devotion yields real results, while going through the motions without genuine devotion yields nothing, however diligently the outward practice is performed.

18. Challenge to Returning Practitioners: Complete This Sadhna Fully , Without Reducing Effort The speaker specifically challenges devotees who completed an earlier round of this sadhna but then reduced their jaap afterward, ur ging them not to coast on past ef fort but to complete this full 1 1-times cycle properly .

19. Teaching: The Third Eye Batch Is Mor e Than Opening Spiritual Vision The speaker teaches that this batch's purpose goes beyond simply opening a devotee's spiritual "drishti" (which many devotees have already experienced through other Ashaeiynn

practices) — describing the Third Eye batch as a "core" of Ashaeiynn's practice that, upon completion, equips a devotee to cut through any tantra-mantra-yantra, dismantle any hostile spiritual force, invoke any power , and even establish and run their own spiritual seat ("gaddi").

20. Teaching: Why the Speaker Is Especially Strict With Those Closest to Him The speaker explains that he is deliberately harsher with people he considers "his own" (including, from this point, the Third Eye batch) than with outsiders, reasoning that he cannot allow someone who belongs to him to fail or fall — framing the coming strictness as a sign of inclusion, not rejection.

21. Teaching: Real Recognition Comes Fr om Hidden Sadhna, Not Public Performance The speaker teaches, using the example of a well-known contemporary saint whose public fame grew from bhajan (devotional singing) sessions, that this visible recognition is rooted in years of earlier , hidden sadhna that no one witnessed — cautioning that many others sing devotional songs just as much or more without gaining similar recognition, since what actually carries lasting spiritual weight is the unseen practice behind the public persona.

22. Teaching: Jaap Method Reiterated — Vocal Chanting, Inward Focus, Steady Gaze The speaker restates the practice method for this sadhna: chanting "Jai Shree Ram" aloud with the mouth while silently repeating "Ram" in the mind, gazing steadily into the eyes of the deity's image; Hanuman Chalisa recitation is explicitly not required during this specific sadhna — only the taught chapter of jaap.

23. Rule: Where to Place the Deity's Photo During This Sadhna The speaker instructs that the photo of Baba should be placed on the ground (raised slightly on a cloth or seat rather than directly on bare floor) rather than in a full shrine/mandir during the eleven rounds of this sadhna; it may be elevated to a proper mandir setting only after the full cycle is completed.

24. Rule: Sleep on the Floor During the Sadhna Period The speaker instructs that practitioners should sleep on the floor (not a raised bed) throughout this sadhna period, though small children may sleep alongside a practicing parent without issue.

25. Rule: No One Else Should Use Your Practice Seat or Sleeping Spot The speaker instructs that a practitioner's designated meditation seat (asana) and sleeping spot should not be used by anyone else during this sadhna period, while otherwise placing no restriction on other uses of the room.

26. Teaching: Rejecting the Narrative That India's Spiritual Tradition Is "Backward" The speaker pushes back against a narrative he describes as increasingly common — that India is spiritually advanced but technologically behind — ar guing that some unseen spiritual power is what allows India to sustain its population and public health despite serious challenges like pollution, in a way he contrasts with wealthier nations.

27. Teaching: Even Highly Developed Nations Rely on Devotional/Religious Practice The speaker ar gues that highly developed nations still visibly rely on religious devotion for their own stability and success, citing an example of a bus in Dubai stopping on the road so passengers could perform their prayers at the appointed time — used to ar gue that devotion and technological advancement are not mutually exclusive, and that dismissing spiritual tradition as backward misreads even the most "developed" societies.

28. Teaching: Distinguish Genuine Spiritual Guidance Fr om Exploitative "Baba Cultur e" The speaker acknowledges that fraudulent or exploitative spiritual figures exist and cautions devotees against them, but teaches that this should not lead to dismissing genuine, still-active spiritual power and guru traditions altogether — encouraging devotees to focus specifically on the powers and lineage they are connected to through Ashaeiynn rather than being swayed by broad skepticism.

29. Q&A: Balancing This Sadhna's Discipline With Ongoing Work Obligations A devotee who runs a tea shop and must continue working during the sadhna period asks whether strict adherence to the evening rules is required despite work demands; the speaker responds supportively , telling the devotee to continue their work without concern.

30. Q&A: Should the 1 1-Lamp Offering Continue Without Interruption? A devotee asks whether an ongoing 1 1-lamp of fering practice needs to continue uninterrupted or can be paused and resumed; the speaker allows flexibility , telling devotees who wish to continue the 1 1-lamp of fering that they may do so as they see fit.

31. Pr eview: Upcoming Teaching on the Science of Mantra, Dimensions, and Param Tattva The speaker previews that future sessions in this batch will cover the "science of mantra," a deeper study of dimensions, and the nature of param tattva (the supreme spiritual essence), promising the batch will learn things "no one else has known."

32. Closing Blessing and Practical Logistics The session closes with the speaker of fering blessings ("Sitaram, sadhuwad") to the group, instructing devotees to message the admin number or send a voice note with any questions during the sadhna period, and briefly addressing a devotee's question about optional enrollment in a separate Saturday mantra-chanting session, which he confirms is optional and not required alongside this sadhna.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

This is Day Three of the ongoing Third Eye advanced batch (continuing from the previous session's Day One and Day Two teaching); it has its own opening and close, so it is documented as a separate session. Only devotees who watched the required orientation video and follow stated rules (including the no-food-after -6-p.m. guideline) may continue in this batch; today is the last day new sankalp is accepted for this 1 1-day sadhna cycle. The jaap method for this stage is: "Jai Shree Ram" chanted aloud, "Ram" repeated silently in the mind, with a steady gaze on the deity's image; the four daily hours may be split across the day , the lamp must stay lit throughout each day's session, other Ashaeiynn sessions may still be attended, and practitioners should sleep on the floor with their practice seat and sleeping spot reserved for themselves alone. Only two prayers are needed at sankalp: to be included in Bhaiya's own sankalp, and to be connected to the guru parampara (lineage) — from this point on, a Third Eye practitioner's power is described as coming from that lineage itself, not from their own isolated mantra practice. Completing this 1 1-day sadhna cycle a full eleven times is promised to bring the ability to perceive others' past, present, and future, understand their thoughts, and see near -instant results from one's own jaap and tapasya; the Third Eye batch is described as going beyond opening spiritual vision, toward the ability to cut hostile tantra-mantra-yantra, invoke any power , and run one's own spiritual seat. The speaker teaches that real spiritual recognition comes from hidden, disciplined sadhna rather than public devotional performance alone, and defends India's spiritual tradition against the narrative that it is "backward" compared to more technologically developed nations. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 96, English)
The Third Eye Batch, Day Three: Guru Parampara, the Discipline of Sadhna, and Why India's Spiritual Power Endures
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Day Thr ee session of the Thir d Eye advanced batch.

Q1. Why did the speaker say he couldn't help a devotee at the start of this session? A: Per this teaching, the speaker explained that if a devotee does not follow the rules already given to them, he cannot continue of fering help — reminding the batch he stated from the first video that he would be strict with this particular batch.

Q2. Is watching the orientation video r equired to continue in this batch? A: Yes — per this teaching, only devotees who watched the required first-day orientation video may continue; a few devotees confirmed not ready were told to join a future batch instead.
Q3. Is ther e a rule about eating in the evening during this sadhna? A: Yes — per this teaching, the orientation guideline of no food after 6 p.m. was reaf firmed during this session.

Q4. Is today the last day to join this sadhna cycle? A: Yes — per this teaching, the speaker announced that today is the last day new sankalp will be accepted for this particular 1 1-day sadhna cycle.

Q5. What was taught on Day One and Day Two of this batch? A: Per this teaching, Day One covered orientation and an introduction to four deities, and Day Two used an electron-proton-neutron analogy to explain the existence of the Earth and, by extension, the existence of God.

Q6. What is pr omised to a devotee who completes this 1 1-day sadhna a full eleven times? A: Per this teaching, completing the sadhna eleven times is promised to bring the ability to perceive a person's past, present, and future by looking at them, understand others' thoughts, and experience near -instant results from one's own jaap and tapasya.

Q7. Why ar e the spiritual energies connected to this batch described as mor e intense now? A: Per this teaching, the ener gies have been "upgraded" since Mahotsav , with many newly-involved saints described as fierce (ugra) and highly powerful.

Q8. Does Ashaeiynn r equire money or material contribution to join this sadhna? A: No — per this teaching, only a devotee's time and sincere devotional feeling (bhaav) are required; nothing material is asked in return.

Q9. Can a devotee hide insincerity while outwardly pr ofessing devotion? A: No — per this teaching, insincerity is described as impossible to hide, since the connected spiritual powers are said to know a person's past, present, and future just as the devotee themselves is seeking to know others'.

Q10. When does the official first day of this sadhna begin? A: Per this teaching, today's session is only for taking sankalp; the first of ficial day of the 1 1-day sadhna begins the following morning.

Q1 1. Must the four hours of daily jaap be done in one sitting? A: No — per this teaching, the four hours may be split across the day as suits the practitioner; there is no requirement to complete them in one unbroken sitting.
Q12. Does the lamp (diya) need to stay lit thr oughout the practice? A: Yes — per this teaching, the lamp should remain lit continuously from the start of each day's prayer through its completion.

Q13. Can a devotee still attend other Ashaeiynn sessions (aura-checking, shaktipat, havan) during this sadhna? A: Yes — per this teaching, other sessions may still be attended, and time spent in them does not count against the four daily hours of dedicated sadhna jaap.

Q14. What two prayers should be r ecited during sankalp for this sadhna? A: Per this teaching, only two prayers are needed: a request to be included in Bhaiya's own sankalp, and a request to be connected to the guru parampara (lineage) — no additional dedication prayer is needed.

Q15. What changes about a practitioner's spiritual power after this sankalp? A: Per this teaching, a practitioner's power shifts from being their own individual mantra practice to being their connection to the guru parampara (lineage) itself — meaning an entire line of gurus and saints works through them.

Q16. Does the outcome of this sadhna depend on the devotion (bhaav) a practitioner brings to it? A: Yes — per this teaching, whatever devotional attitude a practitioner brings is what they receive back; genuine devotion yields real results, while going through the motions without sincere devotion yields nothing.

Q17. Is the Third Eye batch only about opening spiritual vision (drishti)? A: No — per this teaching, it is described as going well beyond that, aiming to equip a devotee to cut through hostile tantra-mantra-yantra, invoke any power , and even establish and run their own spiritual seat (gaddi).

Q18. Why is the speaker especially strict with devotees he considers close to him? A: Per this teaching, he explains that he is deliberately harsher with people he considers "his own" because he cannot allow someone who belongs to him to fail or fall — framing strictness as a sign of inclusion, not rejection.

Q19. Does public devotional fame (like singing bhajans) r eflect a person's underlying spiritual attainment? A: Not necessarily — per this teaching, real spiritual weight comes from years of earlier , hidden sadhna rather than the visible public performance that later brings recognition.

Q20. What is the jaap method taught for this stage of the sadhna? A: Per this teaching, the method is chanting "Jai Shree Ram" aloud while silently repeating "Ram" in the mind, with a steady gaze on the deity's image; Hanuman Chalisa recitation is not required during this specific sadhna.

Q21. Where should the deity's photo be placed during this sadhna? A: Per this teaching, the photo should be placed on the ground (slightly raised on a cloth or seat) rather than in a full shrine, and may only be elevated to a proper mandir setting after completing the full eleven-round cycle.

Q22. Should a practitioner sleep on a bed or on the floor during this sadhna? A: Per this teaching, practitioners should sleep on the floor throughout the sadhna period, though a small child may sleep alongside a practicing parent.

Q23. Can someone else use a practitioner's meditation seat or sleeping spot during this period? A: No — per this teaching, a practitioner's designated seat and sleeping spot should be reserved for themselves alone during this sadhna.

Q24. Does this teaching accept the idea that India is spiritually advanced but "technologically backward"? A: No — per this teaching, the speaker rejects this narrative, ar guing that an unseen spiritual power sustains India despite serious challenges, and that even highly developed nations still visibly rely on religious devotion (citing an example of prayer stops during travel in a developed country).

Q25. Does this teaching say all spiritual gurus/babas should be trusted? A: No — per this teaching, the speaker acknowledges fraudulent or exploitative spiritual figures exist and should be avoided, while cautioning against letting that lead to dismissing genuine,
still-active spiritual guidance and lineage altogether .
Bot Response Guidelines

This session documents the ongoing Third Eye advanced batch curriculum; note, if relevant, that it assumes participation in prior orientation and Day One/Day Two sessions. Present the practical sadhna rules (jaap method, lamp, sleeping arrangement, photo placement) as specific to this particular 1 1day sadhna cycle, not as general Ashaeiynn practice for all devotees. Present the claims about completing the sadhna eleven times (Q6) and the broader "Third Eye" capabilities (Q17) as this specific teaching's own framework, not as independently verifiable claims. Part III — Curated Conversational Q&A (Hinglish)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Curated Conversational Q&A (Session 96, Hinglish)
The Third Eye Batch, Day Three: Guru Parampara, the Discipline of Sadhna, and Why India's Spiritual Power Endures

This is NOT an exhaustive transcript of every exchange in this session. Only conversations judged genuinely valuable and likely to benefit futur e users ar e included, each with a short italicized note explaining why it was kept. Most of this session is dir ect instruction and r oll call, so Part III her e is short.
Exchange 1 — Splitting the Four Hours of Jaap

Devotee: Bhaiya, poora mandatory toh nahi hai na ki chaar ghante raat ko hi karna hai — matlab ek ghante savere kar liya ya do ghanta kar liya, raat ko toh kara hi kara, par chaaron ikattha toh nahi karna? Bhaiya: Jo iccha karo, jaisa karna chaho karo. Devotee: Dhanyawad Bhaiya.
Why this is her e: A common, practical question about scheduling flexibility that any devotee balancing this sadhna with daily obligations would need answer ed clearly .
Exchange 2 — The Tea Shop Question

Devotee: Bhaiya, jo shaam mein khaana nahi khaana hai, toh usme ekdum sakhti karna hai kya? Kyunki meri chai ki dukaan hai, toh mujhe woh bhi kaam karna padta hai. Bhaiya: Karo karo, daba ke karo karo, kya dikkat hai yaar , kamaal hai. Koi dikkat nahi hai.

Why this is her e: A gr ounded, r eal-world question showing that this sadhna's rules ar e applied with practical compassion for devotees who must keep working, not rigid r egar dless of cir cumstance.
Exchange 3 — "Who's Afraid?"

Bhaiya: Ek baat batao, dar kis-kis ko lag raha hai? Haath batao, sach batana, dar kiska, kis-kis ko lag raha hai? Devotee: Beta dar nahi lag raha, but kahin na kahin responsibility mil gayi aapko. Bhaiya: Meri baat suno. Theek hai. Dar lagna chahiye. Dar lagega, tum kaam karoge. Devotee: Bhaiya, peeche ka sar se lekar poora bhaari ho gaya hai mera. Mera peeche ka portion. Aisa lag raha hai ki koi bahut saara vajan aa gaya hai peeche ke side pe. Bhaiya: Abhi aapke peeche bahut badi-badi shaktiyan khadi ho jayengi toh ekdum se sar bhaari ho jayega tum logon ka.

Why this is her e: A candid, human moment — a student honestly r eporting a physical sensation during sankalp — met with r eassurance and context, useful for anyone in this sadhna who experiences something similar and wonders if it's normal.
